targets.name: Barnard's Star
targets.note: A red dwarf 6 light-years away. It crosses our sky faster than any other star.
targets.summary: Barnard's Star moved 9.1 arcsec to the north, a shift equal to 1/205 of the width of the full moon. This red dwarf is 6 light-years away and crosses our sky faster than any other star.

targets.name: Kapteyn's Star
targets.note: A very old star about 13 light-years away, with the second-fastest motion across the sky.
targets.summary: Kapteyn's Star was measured to have moved 8.3 arcsec per year toward the south-east. This is a very old star about 13 light-years away, with the second-fastest motion across the sky.

targets.name: Groombridge 1830
targets.note: A star about 30 light-years away that races across the sky at 7 arcseconds a year.
targets.summary: Groombridge 1830 moved 7.0 arcsec south between the observations. This star is about 30 light-years away and races across the sky at 7 arcseconds a year.

targets.name: Lacaille 9352
targets.note: A red dwarf about 10.7 light-years away in the southern sky.
targets.summary: Lacaille 9352 moved by 8.0 arcsec to the east, a shift equal to 1/233 of the full moon's width. This is a red dwarf about 10.7 light-years away in the southern sky.

targets.name: Wolf 359
targets.note: One of the closest stars to the Sun, about 7.9 light-years away.
targets.summary: Wolf 359 moved by 4.2 arcsec across the sky. This star is one of the closest to the Sun, located about 7.9 light-years away.

targets.name: Teegarden's Star
targets.note: A small red dwarf 12.5 light-years away with Earth-sized planets.
targets.summary: Teegarden's Star moved by 5.1 arcsec over the course of the observations. This small red dwarf is located 12.5 light-years away and hosts Earth-sized planets.

targets.name: WISE J184125.47+095436.5
targets.note: A star that NASA's WISE telescope flagged as variable years earlier. Can SPHEREx see it change?
targets.summary: WISE J184125.47+095436.5 faded by 0.66 magnitudes between September 2025 and September 2026. This star was previously flagged as variable by NASA's WISE telescope, and SPHEREx is now observing it for further changes.

targets.name: Pleiades
targets.note: A young star cluster about 440 light-years away, wrapped in dust that reflects starlight.
targets.summary: No measurable changes were found in the sky across the three observation periods. The Pleiades is a young star cluster about 440 light-years away, wrapped in dust that reflects starlight.

targets.name: Crab Nebula
targets.note: The remains of a star that exploded and was seen from Earth in the year 1054.
targets.summary: No measurable changes were found in the sky view of the Crab Nebula across the available observations. This object is the remains of a star that exploded and was seen from Earth in the year 1054.

targets.name: Orion Nebula
targets.note: A cloud 1,300 light-years away where new stars are forming.
targets.summary: No measurable changes were detected in the Orion Nebula across the observed periods. This cloud is 1,300 light-years away where new stars are forming.
